item.description:
Operational Capabilities

The Doctrine

I believe in forensic truth. Tools are fallible; raw data is not. My approach to security is grounded in the command line, deep-dive artifact analysis, and the understanding that every adversary leaves a trace if you know how to look.

Core Competencies

  • Advanced Incident Response: Full-lifecycle management of high-severity breaches. I don’t just alert on threats; I hunt, contain, and eradicate them.
  • Digital Forensics: Expert-level analysis of disk images and memory. I prefer manual verification (hex editors, timeline analysis) over trusting a “magic button” tool.
  • Malware Analysis: Reverse engineering malicious binaries to understand capabilities, C2 protocols, and intent.
  • Threat Intelligence: Converting abstract indicators into actionable operational intelligence.

The Toolkit

  • Forensics: Plaso, EnCase, FTK, Volatility.
  • Terminal: Bash, PowerShell, Vim (heavily customized for log parsing).
  • Infrastructure: Windows Server Internals, RHEL/Debian, Cloud Security Architecture.

Certification History

  • GREM (Reverse Engineering Malware)
  • GCFA (Forensic Analyst)
  • GCIH (Incident Handler)
  • GCTI (Cyber Threat Intelligence)

item.title: LockBit 3.0 Ransomware via Phishing Email
item.description:
Executive Summary

On August 15, 2024, Acme Co. experienced a LockBit 3.0 ransomware attack that encrypted approximately 2.3TB of data across three file servers and 47 mapped network drives. The initial infection vector was a malicious ZIP attachment opened by an employee accessing personal Gmail on their corporate workstation (ACME-WKS-0247).

The adversary achieved initial execution at 13:47 UTC, established persistence, disabled Windows Defender and Volume Shadow Copy Service, and began encryption at 14:18 UTC. The attack was detected 5 minutes into the encryption phase when multiple users reported inaccessible files.

item.title: Visualizing Forensics: The TLN Vim Profile
item.description:
The Problem: Timeline Fatigue

In major incident response engagements, “Excel fatigue” is real. staring at a CSV with 5 million rows from log2timeline is a quick way to miss lateral movement.

The Solution: A Vim-Based Workflow

I developed a workflow to process disk images while keeping the analysis environment lightweight and keyboard-centric.

1. Extraction

Processing the raw disk image using Plaso to generate a bodyfile.

2. Conversion

Converting the bodyfile to the TLN (Time Line) format. This format is superior for quick scanning because of its epoch-time sorting and pipe-delimited structure.
